name: Hello, World!
prompt: Print exactly `Hello, World!` followed by a newline.
shows: Program skeleton, entry point, and output.

name: Factorial
prompt: Define a recursive function factorial(n) and print factorial(10). If the language (or the historical dialect shown) has no recursion, use a loop and say so in notes.

name: FizzBuzz
prompt: For i from 1 to 15 print Fizz for multiples of 3, Buzz for multiples of 5, FizzBuzz for both, otherwise the number — one per line.
expected_output:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz
Fizz
7
8
Fizz
Buzz
11
Fizz
13
14
FizzBuzz

name: Map & filter
prompt: Take the numbers 1..10, keep the even ones, square them, and print the result on one line as `4 16 36 64 100` — using the language's most idiomatic collection style (map/filter, comprehension, array ops, query, loop...).

name: Shapes
prompt: Model two kinds of shape — Rectangle(width 3, height 4) and Triangle(base 10, height 3) — each with an area operation, using the language's idiomatic data modelling (classes, ADTs + pattern matching, records, structs + interfaces, prototypes, multimethods, tables...). Print `Rectangle: 12` then `Triangle: 15` (integer formatting).
shows: Data modelling and polymorphism: OOP vs ADTs vs records.

name: Signature idiom
prompt: A short program (under ~25 lines) showing off what is most distinctive about this language — its signature idea. Give it a `title` and document its exact expected_output.
shows: The idea this language is famous for.
